intro: Yemen was once 'Arabia Felix', happy Arabia, rich from incense and spices. Today it is suffering from one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

chapters.title: Kingdoms of incense
text: Ancient kingdoms such as Saba (Sheba), Qataban and Himyar grew rich trading frankincense and myrrh. The Marib Dam, built around 2,700 years ago, watered a huge oasis. The Bible and the Qur'an tell of the Queen of Sheba.
The Romans called the region Arabia Felix because of its green terraced mountains and wealth.

chapters.title: Islam and imams
text: Yemen accepted Islam in the 600s. Zaydi imams ruled the northern highlands for about a thousand years. The Ottomans controlled parts of the country at different times, and Britain held the port of Aden from 1839.
Yemen was the first great exporter of coffee, shipped from the port of Mocha, which gave its name to a drink.

highlight.title: Coffee
highlight.text: Coffee drinking as we know it began in Yemen's Sufi monasteries in the 1400s.

chapters.title: Division, unity and war
text: North Yemen became a republic after a revolution in 1962; South Yemen became independent from Britain in 1967 and later communist. They united in 1990.

After protests in 2011, Ali Abdullah Saleh stepped down. In 2014 the Houthi movement took the capital, Sanaa, and in 2015 a Saudi-led coalition intervened. The war has caused hunger, disease and the displacement of millions.
